title: Minimax Estimation of the Latent-Cutoff Effect in Regression Discontinuity with Noisy Scores
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered compact-positive-band minimax theorem is subfield below the field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: it does not characterize the practically important transition when sigma tends to zero
its potentially enormous thresholds and coefficients come without conditioning, runtime, or numerical evidence
the general reverse modulus comparison and sharp efficiency loss remain open
paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'
proof_attempt_summary: The original uniform-to-zero phase theorem stalled on a one-sided observation inequality and a matching legal lower witness. A narrower compact-positive-noise theorem proved a matched minimax rate with an explicit finite shifted-Legendre estimator and same-class Bernoulli lower construction; both final math and decision reviews passed. The final tier gate rated the delivered paper subfield because the shrinking-noise transition, practical numerical behavior, and general reverse-modulus comparison remain open.
tldr: For the latent-cutoff effect \(\theta(P)=\mu_1(0)-\mu_0(0)\), the minimax expected absolute risk is \(\{\log\log(en)/\log(en)\}^\beta\) uniformly on every fixed compact positive-noise band \([\underline\sigma,\sigma_0]\). An explicit side-supported clipped-ratio estimator attains this order: its weight is a finite shifted-Legendre polynomial of degree \(D_{m_n}=\lceil A m_n\rceil\), computable from \(n\), the known \(\sigma\), the fixed lower band edge, and the fixed class constants. A common-amplitude tapered-Jacobi Bernoulli pair gives the matching same-class lower bound. At the separate endpoint \(\sigma=0\), the risk is of order \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\).
gap: No checked result matches the pointwise latent-cutoff risk across zero, shrinking, and fixed Gaussian noise when assignment uses the observed noisy score, no auxiliary true-score sample is available, each arm-specific first-moment convolution subdensity is available only on its assignment half-line, and the compactly supported latent density is unknown and only locally smooth.
fill: The project evaluates that modulus, derives its explicit transition boundaries, joins a direct local-polynomial endpoint to the positive-noise side-supported optimizer, proves a same-class Bernoulli converse, and separates the latent effect from the conventional observed-score discontinuity.
